question: True or false: the train that set the 2007 wheeled rail speed record ran on bigger wheels than service TGVs?
answer: True. The V150 trainset that reached 574.8 km/h on the Paris–Strasbourg high-speed line had wheels 1,092 mm across instead of the standard 920 mm, and the overhead line was raised from 25,000 to 31,000 volts. Service trains there run at up to 320 km/h. The record train was an instrument built for one run.
move: Ask how far a record machine differs from the one you can use.
trap: Assuming a record train is an ordinary train pushed harder.
reference: Alstom, SNCF and RFF, V150 world rail speed record, press release, 3 April 2007
